title: The Half Reward (हिन्दी)
summary: A greedy gatekeeper demands half the reward of a poor poet presenting verses to the Emperor. Birbal ensures the guard receives exactly what he asked for. [HI]
full_text:
A brilliant but destitute poet named Keshav traveled from Varanasi to Agra, having composed an epic poem celebrating Emperor Akbar's justice and wisdom. Arriving at the southern gate of the Agra Fort, he was stopped by an arrogant and corrupt sentry named Murad.

Seeing the poet's scroll and humble attire, Murad blocked the archway with his spear: 'Only nobles enter here, beggar! Unless you promise me in writing that you will give me exactly half of whatever gift the Emperor bestows upon you today, you shall rot outside this gate!'

Having no choice, the poet agreed and signed a parchment slip.

Keshav was admitted into the Diwan-i-Khas. He recited his magnificent verses with such passion, melody, and eloquence that the entire court was spellbound. Akbar was so delighted that he exclaimed: 'Poet, your words are like drops of liquid gold! Ask for whatever you desire, and it shall be yours!'

Keshav bowed low: 'Your Majesty, I ask for only one reward: grant me sixty lashes with a heavy bamboo cane upon my back!'

The entire court fell silent in horror. Akbar thought the poet had lost his mind: 'Are you mad? I wish to reward you with rubies or gold, and you ask for stripes of a cane?'

'It is my heartfelt wish, Sire,' Keshav insisted.

Akbar reluctantly commanded the royal guard to administer the lashes, but ordered them struck gently. After thirty lashes had been struck over a thick padded jacket, the poet raised his hand:

'Halt, Your Majesty! I have a business partner at the palace gate. Sentry Murad forced me to sign a contract swearing to surrender exactly half of my reward to him before allowing me inside! He must receive his rightful thirty lashes!'

Akbar's face turned crimson with rage. He had Murad dragged into the hall, showed him the signed parchment, and commanded the executioner:

'Administer the remaining thirty lashes to this corrupt sentry with full force, and dismiss him from imperial service forever!'

After the crooked guard had been whipped and hauled away, Akbar presented poet Keshav with one thousand gold mohurs and a horse, while Birbal remarked that honesty always finds a way to turn extortion into retribution.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Half Reward"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
